[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Advanced DataFrame Operations and Functions in Apache Spark"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Apache Spark DataFrames provide a rich set of functions for manipulating large-scale structured data. While basic operations like filtering and selecting are straightforward, advanced analytics often require window functions, complex aggregations, and custom user-defined functions."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Window Functions for Analytical Queries"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Window functions operate on a group of rows, referred to as a window, and return a single value for every input row. They are essential for running totals, moving averages, and ranking."},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
from pyspark.sql.window import Window
from pyspark.sql import functions as F

spark = SparkSession.builder.appName("AdvancedDataFrameOps").getOrCreate()

# Sample DataFrame creation
data = [("Sales", "Alice", 100), ("Sales", "Bob", 200), ("Engineering", "Charlie", 300), ("Engineering", "David", 400)]
df = spark.createDataFrame(data, ["Department", "Employee", "Salary"])

# Define window specification
windowSpec = Window.partitionBy("Department").orderBy(F.desc("Salary"))

# Apply dense_rank
ranked_df = df.withColumn("rank", F.dense_rank().over(windowSpec))
ranked_df.show()"},{"order":6,"type":"subheading","text":"Working with Complex Data Types"},{"order":7,"type":"paragraph","text":"Spark DataFrames support complex types like arrays and structs. You can use built-in functions to transform and flatten these structures efficiently."},{"order":8,"type":"code","text":"# Creating a DataFrame with an array column
array_data = [("Alice", ["Java", "Python"]), ("Bob", ["Spark", "Scala"])]
array_df = spark.createDataFrame(array_data, ["Name", "Skills"])

# Using explode to flatten the array
flattened_df = array_df.withColumn("Skill", F.explode("Skills"))
flattened_df.show()"},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"Best Practices for Advanced Operations"},{"order":10,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Always define explicit schemas when reading data to prevent unexpected type inference issues."},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Be cautious with wide transformations like groupBy and window operations, as they trigger expensive shuffles across the network."},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Leverage catalyst optimizer by using built-in Spark SQL functions instead of Python UDFs whenever possible for better performance."}]
